interest: Translated Diet interpellations and State Department memoranda showing Japan's parliament subordinated to military control.
overview: This file comprises U.S. State Department diplomatic records spanning September 1937 to November 1939 that document the 72nd, 73rd, 74th, and convocation of the 75th sessions of the Japanese Imperial Diet during the escalating Second Sino-Japanese War. Through extensive despatches from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and the Tokyo Embassy, telegrams, legislative summaries, official translations of ministerial addresses, and internal State Department memoranda evaluated by officials such as Joseph W. Ballantine, Stanley K. Hornbeck, and Secretary Cordell Hull, the file monitors the transformation of Japan's domestic governance and external posture under the Konoe and Hiranuma Cabinets. Core topics documented include major policy addresses by Prime Minister Fumimaro Konoe and Foreign Minister Koki Hirota, the severance of relations with China's Nationalist Government, emergency multi-billion yen wartime budgets, the passage of sweeping authoritarian economic measures—notably the National General Mobilization Law and the Electric Power Control Law—and diplomatic frictions surrounding the Open Door policy, the Nine-Power Treaty, belligerent rights, third-power interests, and incidents such as the Panay and Ladybird affairs.
